target.name: PreyVR FrameTiming implementation compiled in an offline audit harness

question: Do the reviewed timing counters summarize the complete collection period and measure compositor drops?
claim: The committed counter implementation retains only 512 duration samples while counting over-budget intervals since reset. The compiled control reported a clean 512-interval window and 2000 earlier over-budget intervals. A second control counted 500 threshold overruns without any compositor. These report populations and semantics cannot establish actual compositor drops or a GPU bottleneck verdict.
method: Read the supplied handover and pinned source using git show d0a64f12ff84162a1ecb1fd0be5809ac8ac240e5:<path>; copy exact FrameTiming sources into project evidence. Compile the separate audit with CMake/Visual Studio 18 2026, MSVC 19.50.35729.0. Run empty-data, slow-prefix/fast-tail, quiescent-reset and alternating-threshold controls. Exact configure/build/run commands and output are in verification.txt. Read only the named saved run manifests and logs to corroborate build/runtime/dimensions; did not interact with any process. Author timing tables were not promoted to raw benchmark evidence.

identity.reason: Exact FrameTiming source/header copied from full git commit and compiled; files retained with the audit.

instrument.reason: MSVC-compiled audit passed assertions against known injected durations; exact output and commands retained.

control.reason: Empty input stays invalid; slow prefix and clean recent tail separate populations; reset clears counters; interval jitter illustrates threshold semantics.

scene.reason: Offline counter harness; no in-game scene or headset claim.

restore.reason: No game, runtime, command channel or target binary was modified.

baseline.reason: No vanilla game, real GPU, runtime presentation or headset baseline was measured. Offline instrument controls passed; they do not approve a performance build.

limits: Confirms counter semantics in a synthetic harness and source-level report wiring. Does not confirm or refute whether Prey is CPU-bound, GPU-bound or paced; does not quantify a performance improvement. Re-arm concurrency is a source-proven possible interleaving, not reproduced at runtime. Saved timing responses were absent only from the explicitly inspected log/current-result files. Source identities may be superseded by later edits.

artifacts.role: Scoped review and next experiment; distinguishes source, harness, author and runtime evidence
Compiler identity and successful control output with reproduction commands
Pinned report, timing and command wiring excerpts with source line numbers
Read-only saved run identity and scoped timing-retention checks
Original user-supplied handover; tables are AUTHOR evidence, not raw timing samples

do_not_repeat.approach: Treat rolling-window percentiles plus a cumulative threshold counter as whole-run compositor miss statistics or use ratios of CPU medians to clear GPU/pacing costs.
do_not_repeat.reason: Different populations, no compositor observation, no GPU timestamp measurement, and no per-frame stage pairing.
do_not_repeat.reopen_when: Capture fixed-view repeated controls with consistent epochs/denominators, durable paired CPU/GPU samples and runtime presentation evidence.

next_action: Fix timing epoch synchronization, retention and explicit window/total/period reporting; add asynchronous GPU query spans and compatible vanilla/injected-lanes-off controls. Candidate for the existing playbook profiling/measurement guidance (docs/06-debugging-methodology.md and docs/19-d3d12-and-performance.md); do not promote a Prey bottleneck conclusion or clear a gate.
